"One day, that's it," said Kunal, closing the tutorial tab. "After this, I build something."
"Something like what?" asked Jomon, looking up from his snack.
"An expense tracker. Add an amount, pick a category, see the total."
"You've only watched one video."
"That's why it will break." Kunal opened an empty file. Ten minutes later he groaned. "It says 'undefined'. Why?"
"Did you name the box the same in both places?"
"...No. Two different spellings."
By evening the tracker added amounts and showed a total. It was ugly, but it ran. Kunal leaned back. "That one error taught me more than the last half hour of the video."
"Then do another error," Jomon grinned.

qa.a: Kunal decided to build an expense tracker.

I'm Kishore, and last semester I had to learn a new database tool for my part-time job. My friend Yamini said, 'Stop watching and start making.' So I gave the beginner tutorial exactly one Sunday.
On Monday I began my own thing: a tracker for what I spend on canteen food, auto fare and printouts. First the table wouldn't save, because I had named a column 'date', which the tool keeps for itself. Then my totals came out as zero, because I had stored the amounts as text. Each error sent me to read one small section of the help pages, and each fix stuck in my head far better than any video had.
By Friday the tracker showed my week's spending by category. It looked ugly. It worked, and I understood every line of it.

qa.q: What did Kishore's tracker record spending on?
qa.a: Canteen food, auto fare and printouts.

qa.q: How did Kishore probably feel when the totals came out as zero?
qa.a: Kishore was likely frustrated at first but also curious, since each error led to one small section of the help pages and the fix stuck.

qa.q: Which approach would suit Kishore better if an error could not be solved from the help pages?
qa.a: Post the exact error and the steps already tried to a senior or a forum, so one clear question gets the build moving again.

qa.q: How might Yamini see the ugly but working tracker?
qa.a: Yamini would likely be pleased, since the advice to stop watching and start making led to something Kishore understands line by line.

grounding: Shows a student taking one day of tutorial and then building a spending tracker, learning mostly from fixing its errors.

Mentor log, internship week 2 – Aparna
Uma joined our team knowing nothing about the charting library we use. On Monday she did the official beginner tutorial and nothing else. On Tuesday I suggested a tiny project: a page that tracks the team's shared tea-and-snacks spending. She groaned but started.
By noon she had hit three errors: a missing import, a wrong file path, and a chart that drew every bar at zero. She asked me about the first one only; the other two she traced herself by reading the messages slowly.
On Wednesday she told me she had learnt more from those three errors than from two days of videos. I've asked her to show the tracker at Friday's stand-up, and next week I will pair her with Neeraj on a real ticket.

qa.q: Which three errors did Uma hit by noon on Tuesday?
qa.a: A missing import, a wrong file path, and a chart that drew every bar at zero.

qa.q: What does Uma's groan on Tuesday suggest?
qa.a: Uma was likely reluctant and a little nervous about building before feeling ready, though she later seemed pleased with what the errors taught her.

qa.q: What could Aparna try next to keep Uma learning this fast?
qa.a: Give Uma a real ticket with a partner, as planned, so the learning stays tied to building rather than watching.

qa.q: How might Neeraj experience being paired with Uma next week?
qa.a: Neeraj may find it easier than expected, since Uma already knows how to read error messages and trace most problems alone.

grounding: Shows an intern doing one day of tutorial, then building a small spending tracker and learning mainly from its errors.
